title: cy-manifest v1
description: The App Store submission manifest carried at the root of a Cytoscape Web app archive. One JSON object describing exactly one app. This is a PREVIEW identity: it may change until the first stable identity is issued, after which the official property set and validation envelope are frozen and any change — in either direction — requires a new formatVersion. Canonical validity is this schema PLUS strict raw-JSON validation PLUS the semantic predicates pinned beside it; see cy-manifest-v1.predicates.json.

formatVersion.description: The wire-compatibility major. Rejected before any other property is interpreted.

id.description: The Module Federation container name, the exported CyApp.id and the registry id at once. Never trimmed. The reserved-id list is a predicate, not a schema keyword.

name.description: Display name. Trimmed by the producer; a present untrimmed or empty value is noncanonical.

version.description: Canonical SemVer 2.0.0 without build metadata. Never trimmed. The numeric-identifier magnitude bound is a predicate.

entry.description: The federation entry, relative to the archive root. There is deliberately no url: the Store assigns one when it hosts the bundle.

author.description: Public display name only. An email address never appears here.

repository.description: Canonical credential-free https URL. Shorthands, SSH forms, objects and .git suffixes are source-only and rejected on the wire.

repositoryDirectory.description: Relative POSIX path within the repository. Material for monorepo builds.

homepage.description: Credential-free http(s). Plain http passes the producer boundary because a local development URL is a legitimate package value; the Store's publication profile requires https.

compatibleHostVersions.description: An npm semver range, opaque to the SDK. Range validity is checked where a canonical implementation lives: the Store, and the host.

generator.description: Self-reported diagnostic. Never provenance: the file is generated from developer-controlled input inside an archive the developer can edit afterwards.
